title: Architecture review: {{s10_reports|int}} reports, {{s10_models|int}} models, no owner
seo: Power BI governance and architecture review exercise: assess a messy tenant (reports, semantic models, workspaces), design the target architecture, governance model, consolidation plan and executive recommendation.
summary: The new CEO-sponsored data programme starts with a question: what do we actually have, and what should it look like in a year? You lead the review.
story: You are now leading BI architecture at Northwind. The shared revenue model (Sprint 05), the deployment checks (Sprint 07), the incident process (Sprint 08) and ADR-009 (Sprint 09) all exist, but only for the parts of the estate the BI team touches.
impact: Every unmanaged copy of a model is a possible wrong number, a possible data leak and a refresh that costs capacity. The offsite will decide the data programme's budget; a vague review gets a vague budget.

messages.subject: What do we have?
body: I keep hearing we have "hundreds" of reports and nobody knows which to trust. Before the offsite I want a short, honest picture of where we are, where we should be in a year, and what it takes to get there.
One page for the leadership team, the detail behind it for Elena. Grace
I exported the tenant inventory: workspaces, semantic models, reports with 90-day views. It's messy. Don't propose deleting things you haven't checked; people get very upset about "their" report.
And please don't produce a 40-page governance framework nobody reads.

messages.subject: Ownership
body: From a compliance point of view my main concern is items with personal or financial data that have no named owner. Please flag those.

earlier.intro: In ADR-009 you chose the target platform. This review has to be consistent with it.

consequences.a: You kept the existing models on F64 as they are. The review must therefore tackle duplication model by model: no platform change will consolidate anything for you.
consequences.b: Phase 2 of your plan creates one gold layer in OneLake. Use it: consolidation targets for Sales, Ops and Customer data can all land on the mirrored and gold tables instead of each model loading its own copy.
consequences.c: Your big-bang Lakehouse plan is behind schedule and the team is learning Spark. Be realistic about how much consolidation the same team can do this year.
consequences.d: DirectQuery everywhere has increased load on every source system, and the DBAs now want to restrict BI access. Address this before adding more models.
consequences.default: Most architecture boards choose the phased option (lift to F64, then a gold layer in OneLake). If you haven't recorded ADR-009, assume that.

evidence.title: semantic_models.csv
evidence.desc: Owner, endorsement, revenue measure name, customer table name, RLS and last refresh status.

evidence.title: reports.csv
evidence.desc: Every report with its model and views in the last 90 days.

evidence.title: What already exists from earlier work
body:
- Certified shared sales model with a KPI dictionary (BI-1103).
- Deployment pipeline with post-deployment checks for the BI team's workspaces (INC-2058).
- Incident severity guide and on-call alerts for certified models (INC-2071).
- ADR-009 on the target platform.

tasks: Assess the current state with numbers: duplication, ownership, endorsement, usage, refresh health, revenue and customer definitions.
Design the target: workspace strategy, model consolidation, endorsement and ownership, security, and how it fits ADR-009.
Define a light governance model that people will actually follow.
Plan a 12-month roadmap with phases, owners and risks. Nothing is deleted without checking dependencies and telling owners.
Write the one-page executive recommendation for the offsite.

deliverables.t: Governance model: roles, endorsement criteria, ownership rules

hints: Count before you judge: reports with zero views in 90 days, models without an owner, how many different names Revenue has, how many different customer tables exist, how concentrated usage is.
Usage is very concentrated: a few models serve most viewers. Consolidation should start from what people use, not from what is messy.
Governance that works is short: a few roles, a few rules, and making the certified path the easiest one. Retirement needs a process (owner contact, read-only period, archive), not a delete button.

rubric.good: States the core problem (no ownership and duplicated definitions) rather than listing symptoms.
Current state quantified from the inventory; personal and financial data without owners flagged.
Central vs federated workspaces, consolidation vs leave alone, strict vs light governance, weighed honestly.
Target fits ADR-009 and current platform features (endorsement, domains, lineage, usage metrics, deployment pipelines).
Change resistance, hidden dependencies, capacity and team capacity are addressed with mitigations.
One page, three decisions for leadership, a budget ask and a measurable target for 12 months.

retro: Which number from the inventory will persuade the leadership team most, and why?
Where did you choose federation over central control, and what would make you change that?
What is the first thing you'd do on Monday after the offsite?
